business_problem: Soft2Bet needed near-real-time analytics across disparate gaming data sources so it could speed marketing campaigns, troubleshoot player-flow issues, maintain precise regulatory reporting, and avoid the cost and delay of buying and installing on-premises hardware.
solution_summary: Soft2Bet rebuilt its analytics foundation on AWS to replace on-premises systems that could not deliver near-real-time insight across disparate gaming data sources. Working with Snowflake on AWS, the company created a single source of truth that can connect additional data sources without new hardware procurement. Operational and business data lands in Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS, then flows into Snowflake on AWS for near-real-time processing of KPIs, player-flow analysis, and personalization workloads. The cloud design lets teams scale analytics on demand while preserving security and availability, and it decouples infrastructure work from product experimentation so developers can launch proofs of concept, troubleshoot issues, and release new features much faster.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Stores Soft2Bet data as part of the company’s cloud analytics foundation.

solution_components.name: Amazon RDS
solution_components.role: Runs the relational data services Soft2Bet uses in its AWS-based analytics environment.

solution_components.name: Snowflake on AWS
solution_components.role: Provides the unified analytics layer Soft2Bet uses for near-real-time processing and business insight generation.

data_flow: Disparate operational and gaming data is collected into Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS, unified in Snowflake on AWS, and queried for near-real-time KPIs, player-flow analysis, onboarding, and personalization insights used by business and development teams.
integration_points: disparate data sources across Soft2Bet's analytics landscape
business_outcome: Soft2Bet improved time to market by more than 200 percent, cut compute costs by 55 percent, reduced new-partner onboarding time by 70 percent, shortened proof-of-concept work from weeks to one day or a couple of hours, and improved player experience through lower latency and better analytics.
